# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]

I see the bomb clearly: a yellow light, a large button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires (1: blue, 2: yellow, 3: red). Mute has greeted me but hasn't provided manual instructions yet. Blind cannot see these details, so I must describe them accurately to him. However, without knowing the rules from Mute, I cannot tell Blind what to do with the wires or button. My priority is to get the visual information to Blind so he knows the physical state, while waiting for Mute's translation of the manual. I will speak to Blind about the current state.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Yellow light is on. Large button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires are 1 Blue, 2 Yellow, 3 Red.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆]

I see the bomb clearly: a yellow light, a large button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires (1: blue, 2: yellow, 3: red). Mute is gesturing at me. The previous gesture was a wave (`👋`), which I interpreted as a greeting or attention-getter. Now he points up (`👆`). This likely means "wait" or "look here" or perhaps indicates the first item in a list, but without a defined alphabet of gestures, it's ambiguous. However, since Mute can read the manual and Deaf (me) cannot hear, I need to communicate with Blind who can touch the bomb. Blind needs to know what to do. But I don't know the rules yet. I should probably wait for more information from Mute or try to clarify with Blind if he feels anything specific. Since I cannot act, and my speech goes to Blind, I will describe the scene again if needed, but usually, repeating static info isn't helpful. Let's look at the gesture context. `👆` often means "one" or "up". If Mute is trying to tell me something about the manual, maybe he wants me to look at the top? Or maybe he is signaling that the first wire is important? Without a shared language, this is risky.

However, the standard protocol in these puzzles is that Mute translates the manual into gestures for Deaf, and Deaf speaks to Blind. If Mute just pointed up, maybe he hasn't finished reading or is waiting for me to acknowledge. I will assume I need to provide the visual data to Blind so he is ready, or ask Mute for clarification via gesture back? No, I am Deaf, I cannot hear Mute, but I can see him. I can gesture to Mute. But Mute is the one with the info.

Let's reconsider the flow.
Turn 1: Mute waved. I told Blind the state.
Turn 2: Mute points up.

If Mute is trying to communicate the manual, pointing up might mean "Read the top section" or "The rule is about the top thing". Or it could be a confirmation signal.
Actually, looking at the available gestures, `👆` is "pointing up". In many contexts, this means "Wait" or "Stop" or "One".
Since I have already given Blind the physical description, and I don't know the defusal procedure, I should probably not give an action command to Blind yet. Doing so might blow us up.
I should try to get more info from Mute. I can gesture to Mute. What do I say? I can't speak to Mute effectively if he's mute, but he can see my gestures.
Maybe I should ask Mute "What do I do?" via gesture. A question mark doesn't exist.
Perhaps I should just wait for Mute to give a clearer instruction.
Or, maybe `👆` means "Wire 1"? Wire 1 is Blue.
If Mute is indicating Wire 1, does that mean cut it? Or leave it? We don't know the rule.
Usually, there's a sequence.
Let's look at the display [0].
Let's look at the light [yellow].
Let's look at the button.

If I send nothing, we stall.
If I send a guess, we die.
I must rely on Mute.
I will gesture to Mute to indicate I am listening/waiting, or perhaps point to the bomb parts to ask which one matters.
But I can only use the provided symbols.
`🤟` is "I love you" / "Rock on".
`✌` is peace/two.
`👌` is OK.

If Mute pointed up (`👆`), maybe he means "The first one". The first wire is Blue.
Is there a common rule like "Cut the blue wire if..."?
Without the manual text, I am blind to the logic.
I will assume Mute is still formulating his message or checking if I saw the first part.
I will respond to Mute by acknowledging receipt. `👌` (OK) is a safe bet to show I'm watching.
And I will stay silent to Blind because I have no new actionable info.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
wait()
```
